speechWorkerDecouplingProof.summary: The operator's real Windows report (after Phase 3.8.7.1's model installed successfully) showed app slowness, poor/repetitive transcription, empty Intelligence Feed, and intermittent NO SIGNAL. Root-caused (see docs/phase-3-8-7-2-audit.md) to Whisper inference running synchronously on cpal's real-time audio capture callback thread, blocking both real-time audio servicing and the speech_engine mutex the UI's own 3-second status poll also needed.
speechWorkerDecouplingProof.fix: handle_audio_chunk moved off the audio callback thread onto a dedicated speech worker thread (mirroring the already-proven acoustic-worker pattern), fed via an unbounded channel so the real-time audio callback never blocks or drops a chunk.
speechWorkerDecouplingProof.directBinaryProof: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings against the extracted cip-desktop.exe finds the mangled symbol for cip_desktop_lib::commands::spawn_speech_worker - direct proof this fix is genuinely compiled into this exact binary, not just present in source.
speechWorkerDecouplingProof.sermonContentCrossDomainFinding: Confirmed, separately, that Sermon/Content/Cross-Domain Intelligence are not wired to the live audio path at all - a pre-existing, already-documented architectural boundary (Phase 3.8's own ServiceReplay screen exists for this reason), not a regression and not fixed this phase.

backpressureProof.summary: The operator's real Windows report after Phase 3.8.7.2's worker-thread fix confirmed genuine improvement (transcription active, audio arriving) but CIP still became slow over extended listening, transcript remained poor/repetitive, and intermittent NO SIGNAL persisted. Re-auditing the actual current code (docs/phase-3-8-7-3-audit.md) confirmed the operator's own hypothesis: the speech channel (`mpsc::channel::<AudioChunk>()`, start_listening) was genuinely unbounded - if Whisper inference ever takes longer than the ~3s of audio each inference window represents, the backlog grows without limit, and the worker falls permanently further behind live audio.
backpressureProof.fix: A shared `pending_ms: Arc<AtomicU64>` tracks the wall-clock duration of audio queued but not yet fed to the engine (milliseconds, not raw chunk count, since chunk size/rate varies by capture device). start_listening's sink closure increments it on send; spawn_speech_worker decrements it on dequeue. When the remaining backlog crosses OVERLOAD_THRESHOLD_MS (10s), the worker drains and discards the entire queued backlog plus WhisperSpeechEngine's own internal buffer (new SpeechEngine::discard_buffered_audio() trait method) rather than grinding through an ever-more-stale FIFO - this was chosen over a plain bounded/drop-newest channel specifically because that design would still leave the worker permanently behind, never catching up to live audio.
backpressureProof.secondaryFixes: (1) The inferences-attempted counter previously counted every feed_audio call to a ready engine, not just the ~1-in-300 that actually trigger a real whisper.cpp inference pass - fixed via a new SpeechEngine::last_feed_triggered_inference() trait method, checked after each feed_audio call. (2) All four status-poll call sites (get_pilot_diagnostics, start_listening, stop_listening, get_live_status) locked speech_engine's mutex just to read is_ready() - the same mutex the worker holds for the full duration of a blocking Whisper inference - fixed by caching the fact once at construction (AppState::speech_ready), which never changes after that for either existing engine. (3) A low-severity race where a speech worker whose channel closed mid-inference could write output into a newer listening session after a rapid stop/start - fixed via a listening_generation counter checked before any non-empty result is emitted/persisted.
backpressureProof.newDiagnostics: SpeechRuntimeDiagnostics gained queuePendingMs, queueHighWaterMs, overloadEvents, audioMsDroppedOverload, lastInferenceDurationMs/maxInferenceDurationMs/avgInferenceDurationMs, lastTranscriptPipelineDurationMs, and a derived overloadState (normal/busy/falling_behind/overloaded) - all surfaced in the System Diagnostics panel's new 'Speech pipeline health' section, so the operator can directly answer whether audio is backing up, whether inference is keeping up, and whether the app is actively shedding stale audio.
backpressureProof.directBinaryProof: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings against the extracted cip-desktop.exe finds the mangled symbols for cip_desktop_lib::commands::spawn_speech_worker, cip_desktop_lib::commands::handle_audio_chunk, cip_desktop_lib::commands::saturating_sub_u64, and both new SpeechEngine trait method overrides (WhisperSpeechEngine's discard_buffered_audio/last_feed_triggered_inference) - direct proof this phase's fix is genuinely compiled into this exact binary. classify_overload/chunk_duration_ms (small pure functions) were inlined by the release-mode optimizer, as expected, and are instead verified via 10 dedicated unit tests run as part of this phase's regression suite.
backpressureProof.notImplementedThisPhase: Extended-overload (Test C) and stop-during-inference (Test E) real-thread integration scenarios could not be exercised via automated test in this container - consistent with this codebase's own established testing boundary (commands.rs's test module: command tests stop short of standing up a full tauri::test::mock_builder() harness). liveIntelligenceRouterProof.summary: Phase 3.8.7.4's audit found Sermon/Service Phase/Music-text intelligence to be complete, tested engines that were never called from the live speech pipeline - each deliberately built manual-command-only since Phase 2.1-2.6. This phase connects them for the first time via a Live Intelligence Router, and separately bounds Whisper's raw ~3s-per-window transcript output into 12-20s logical segments before anything downstream (Bible detection included) ever sees it.
liveIntelligenceRouterProof.segmentation: New apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/segmentation.rs::TranscriptSegmenter accumulates consecutive raw Whisper-window segments' text until the span reaches a 15s target (the middle of the operator's 12-20s band, landing between 15-18s in practice given Whisper's fixed ~3.0s cadence). Owned exclusively by one speech-worker thread per listening session. Resets on Phase 3.8.7.3's own overload-drain (preventing pre/post-overload text splicing) and force-flushes any partial window when stop_listening closes the channel (previously, any sub-threshold buffered text was simply lost on stop).
liveIntelligenceRouterProof.router: commands.rs::route_segment_to_live_intelligence_engines runs immediately after handle_final_transcript succeeds, on the exact same bounded segment. Calls crate::sermon::analyze_and_queue, crate::service::analyze_and_queue, and music::analyze_and_queue unchanged - the identical functions each manual Tauri command already called, with identical event emissions (SermonFindingDetected/SermonStateChanged/SermonThemeChanged/SermonStructureUpdated, ServicePhaseChanged/ServiceAnomalyDetected, MusicFindingDetected) and timeline records. No new engine logic, no new database schema, no new event contracts, no new Tauri commands - only a new caller.
liveIntelligenceRouterProof.prayerAndWorshipCoverage: Neither is a separate engine: PrayerPoint is a SermonElementKind Sermon Intelligence already detects internally, and ServicePhase::Worship is a phase Service Intelligence already detects internally (both confirmed in docs/phase-3-8-7-4-audit.md). Routing Sermon+Service therefore surfaces Prayer/Worship findings with zero additional code.
liveIntelligenceRouterProof.deliberatelyExcluded: Cross-Domain Correlation and Content Intelligence remain manual-only, per their own explicit 'never automatic' doc comments (a considered Phase 2.4/2.7/2.8 design decision this router does not reverse). Automatic Altar Call detection remains unimplemented - SermonSectionKind::AltarCall exists only as an operator-assignable label with no phrase detector.

overloadSegmenterFixProof.trigger: The operator's real Windows diagnostics for the Phase 3.8.7.5/3.8.7.6 artifact showed 'Nothing transcribed yet' and 'Transcript pipeline: last n/a' despite 21/21 successful Whisper inferences, with exactly 21 overload events (a 1:1 match, not a coincidence) and an average inference duration of 14,991ms against a 10-second overload threshold.
overloadSegmenterFixProof.rootCause: spawn_speech_worker (commands.rs) is single-threaded: while blocked inside one Whisper inference, CPAL keeps depositing new audio chunks into the channel, so the backlog counter climbs by roughly that inference's own wall-clock duration. On hardware where a single inference alone exceeds OVERLOAD_THRESHOLD_MS (10s), the very next dequeue after every successful inference hits the overload branch, which was unconditionally calling segmenter.reset() (Phase 3.8.7.5) - discarding the text that inference just produced before it could ever reach the 15s accumulation target and flush. See docs/phase-3-8-7-7-audit.md for the full trace and arithmetic.
overloadSegmenterFixProof.fix: A new consecutive_overloads counter (commands.rs, owned exclusively by the speech worker thread) tracks overload crossings since the worker was last caught up - reset to 0 on every normal dequeue. A new pure function should_reset_segmenter_on_overload(consecutive_overloads) only returns true at >= 2 (backlog still elevated on the very next dequeue, immediately after already draining once - genuine sustained overload). A single isolated crossing (the case on this operator's hardware) now preserves the segmenter's already-accumulated text; the stale audio backlog itself is still discarded unconditionally either way, unchanged from Phase 3.8.7.3's original design. OVERLOAD_THRESHOLD_MS itself was NOT changed, per the operator's own explicit instruction not to blindly raise it.
overloadSegmenterFixProof.directBinaryProof: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings against the extracted cip-desktop.exe finds the exact log string '%speech worker overloaded: discarded ~' (the overload branch's own log::warn!, now gated by the new consecutive-overload logic before it reaches segmenter.reset()) and the mangled symbols for commands::handle_audio_chunk, commands::finalize_and_route_segment, and segmentation::TranscriptSegmenter::push/flush_remaining/reset, all still present. should_reset_segmenter_on_overload itself (a small pure function, single call site) was inlined by the release-mode optimizer - the same pattern already established for classify_overload in Phase 3.8.7.3 and the router's own dispatch functions in Phase 3.8.7.5 - and is instead verified via two new dedicated unit tests (should_not_reset_segmenter_on_the_first_isolated_overload_crossing, should_reset_segmenter_once_overload_persists_across_consecutive_dequeues), both passing as part of this phase's regression suite (248/248 cip-desktop tests, up from 246).

sermonHarvestProof.trigger: The user shared the project's original master architecture document (the same specification this codebase has been built against since Phase 0) plus example videos, and asked to continue building out the remaining vision, explicitly authorizing all five identified gaps: multi-screen presentation output, semantic/paraphrase Bible detection, Sermon Harvest, real audio fingerprinting, and multi-language support - with Sermon Intelligence kept strict/evidence-only rather than adopting the document's LLM-based generative framing. Sermon Harvest was sequenced first because it required zero new dependencies, zero new detection logic, and zero new AI - it only assembles data this application already captures through five separately-tested pipelines.
sermonHarvestProof.design: harvest_sermon(conn, findings, sermon) (new module apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/harvest.rs) is a pure aggregation function with no detection logic of its own: it does not classify text, does not invent a title/summary when one is absent, and runs no new pass over the transcript. It reads back sections (persistence::list_sermon_sections), elements (every non-rejected IntelligenceFinding with domain==Sermon and sermon_id==Some(sermon.id) from the in-memory FindingQueue), scripture (every Suggestion for the sermon's service), transcript (bounded 5,000 segments), and timeline (bounded 5,000 entries) into one SermonHarvest bundle.
sermonHarvestProof.scopeBoundaryStatedHonestly: IntelligenceFinding::sermon_id linkage lives only in the in-memory FindingQueue, never persisted to the database - a deliberate Phase 2.0 design already documented in docs/phase-3-8-7-6-live-intelligence-integration-audit.md. This means Harvest only ever works for the currently active sermon, in the same app session it was delivered in. The Tauri command calls active_sermon_or_error (the same guard every other active-sermon-scoped command already uses) and refuses cleanly instead of returning a misleadingly incomplete elements: [] bundle for a past/restarted session. A past-session harvest remains a real future need, not attempted this phase.

displayRegistryProof.trigger: Following Phase 3.10.1's pure architecture audit (performed at the user's explicit request, given how much Windows-specific debugging the presentation window pipeline had already been through), the user gave a fully detailed Phase 3.10.2 specification: give each physical monitor a stable session identity, let the operator assign it a role, persist the assignment, and place the presentation window on the assigned monitor - with an explicit instruction not to touch the proven Windows-safe window-creation pipeline itself.
displayRegistryProof.twoDistinctRoleConcepts: DisplayScreen (Phase 3.10: which content stream/window - Stage/Confidence/Lobby) and the new DisplayRole (this phase: which role a physical monitor plays - Unassigned/Operator/Projector/Stage/Confidence/Lobby) are kept as two separate enums, connected only by an explicit bridge function display_registry::screen_role (DisplayScreen::Stage maps to DisplayRole::Projector) - chosen to avoid silently conflating window identity with monitor role.
displayRegistryProof.honestMonitorIdentity: Tauri exposes no real OS-level stable monitor id. compute_monitor_id prefers the OS-reported name, falling back to a position/resolution fingerprint (unnamed@x,y-WxH) - documented as CIP's own best-effort session identity, not a hardware serial number claim.
displayRegistryProof.provenPipelineUntouched: open_display_window's async-command/build ordering and its #[cfg(target_os = "windows")] resize-nudge workaround are structurally unchanged from Phase 3.8.4 - the function only gained an Option<MonitorPlacement> parameter. No assigned role (or a disconnected assigned monitor) reproduces the exact pre-3.10.2 unpositioned 1280x720 window, satisfying the user's explicit 'single-display machines keep working exactly as before' requirement.
displayRegistryProof.dpiCorrectPlacementFix: Monitor's position/size are physical pixels; WebviewWindowBuilder::position/inner_size expect logical pixels. Placement is converted via Tauri's own PhysicalPosition/PhysicalSize::to_logical rather than a hand-rolled division, avoiding an off-by-scale-factor bug on a non-100%-scaled monitor. The pre-existing Windows resize-nudge workaround, previously hardcoded to 1280x720, now consumes the same logical_size actually used to build the window - fixing a latent defect that would have silently fought new placement sizing on Windows specifically.
displayRegistryProof.oneDeliberateUpsertTable: display_role_assignments uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, the one deviation from this project's append-only-log convention for every other table, because role assignment has current-value (not one-row-per-event) semantics - documented explicitly in the migration file. Storage is global (not service-scoped), matching the Phase 3.6 saved_scriptures precedent.
displayRegistryProof.noLiteralFullscreen: This phase positions/sizes the window to the monitor's full bounds but does not call a platform fullscreen API - judged a separate, riskier decision than monitor-fill positioning, documented as a known limitation rather than silently decided.

provenance.builtDuring: Phase 3.8.6 (Windows Whisper Build & Packaging Audit) - the operator's Phase 3.8.5 real-Windows re-test confirmed audio capture now genuinely works (SIGNAL CAPTURED, correct listening lifecycle) but isolated the remaining blocker to transcription itself ('SPEECH ERROR'). The audit (docs/phase-3-8-6-audit.md) confirmed the root cause the operator suspected: no Windows build in this project's history has ever been compiled with the `whisper` Cargo feature, so no prior installer could ever transcribe regardless of hardware. Compiling with --features whisper for this exact cross-compilation target (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, from Linux) hit two independent, real, verified toolchain/upstream defects that had to be fixed before a working build was even possible: (1) whisper.cpp's vendored `ggml` CMake build unconditionally strips the 'lib' prefix from its own static library output for any Windows target (assuming MSVC naming), but the actual linker here is MinGW's GNU ld, which requires the Unix 'libX.a' convention for a plain -lX flag - so ggml.a/ggml-base.a/ggml-cpu.a were built but never found; (2) this container's default x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc/g++ alternative is the win32-threading-model variant, but whisper.cpp/ggml link against pthread and expect POSIX threading, producing 'undefined reference to __mingwthr_key_dtor' at final link - fixed by switching to the already-installed posix-threads alternative via update-alternatives. Neither fix touches the vendored whisper-rs-sys/ggml/whisper.cpp source; see scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh for the exact, repeatable two-pass build process and docs/phase-3-8-6-windows-whisper-build.md for full root-cause evidence. Separately, the audit also found and fixed a real, previously-undocumented defect that would have blocked correct transcription even with the feature/model both present: `integrations/audio` delivers AudioChunks at the capture device's own native sample rate and never resamples (by design - see its module docs), but WhisperSpeechEngine hardcoded a 16kHz assumption and the one consumer that needed to convert (handle_audio_chunk) never did - so a real Windows device negotiating 44.1kHz/48kHz (the norm for consumer WASAPI devices like Stereo Mix/Microphone Array) would have fed audio to Whisper at roughly 3x the wrong rate. Fixed by adding SpeechEngine::required_sample_rate_hz() (a new default trait method, Some(16_000) only for WhisperSpeechEngine) and a linear-interpolation resampler at the one call site that needs it. Also fixed: the real underlying model-load/inference error text (already computed by WhisperSpeechEngine and SpeechEngineError, but discarded after logging) is now retained in AppState and surfaced through the existing get_pilot_diagnostics command/System Diagnostics panel (feature compiled, model loaded, chunks received, last chunk sample rate, inferences attempted/succeeded, real last-error text) instead of the generic 'SPEECH ERROR' notice alone.

releaseCandidateStatement:
This is the Phase 25 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (Session Black Box - downloadable post-test report). The operator's own request, verbatim: "Can it have a 'blackbox', like after testing I should be able to download file that will report everything that happens during the testing period ... so that you'll not be guessing when I give a half report." The gap: every prior diagnostic surface was either live and ephemeral (get_pilot_diagnostics, gone once CIP closes) or a summary of counts (get_service_report's SuggestionStats/DetectionKindCount/TimelineCategoryCount - "12 suggestions, 3 errors" with no way to see which suggestions or what the errors actually said). This phase adds export_session_report, bundling the full transcript, the full timeline (every individual event, not just per-category counts), every suggestion, and every quality-tier correction (both original and corrected text) into one downloadable JSON file, plus a plain-text human_summary paragraph composed from the same data - meant to be pasted directly into a chat message. The existing Phase 5.1 get_service_report also gained the quality-tier and audio-error diagnostic fields it was honestly missing, for free. Full Environment A regression (fmt/clippy/test in both feature configs - 381/381 backend tests, up from 373; frontend typecheck/lint/test/build) passes clean. Two symbol-regression deviations this rebuild (build_bible_detection_analytics and retry_paraphrase_or_semantic_with_fuller_context), both investigated via git diff and nm/demangling and confirmed benign codegen/inlining artifacts with zero source change to any implicated function. Environment C for the wider dual-tier pipeline remains open - this phase's own artifact is what a real Windows-hardware test would use to close it, but the export feature itself has not yet been exercised on real hardware either. Prior release candidate history: This is the Phase 24.3.2 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (quality-tier backlog visibility status label). Continuing directly from the operator's own follow-up direction after Phase 24.3.1: "Fix the backlog visibility status label next." The gap: SpeechQualityDiagnostics.jobs_dropped_backlog (Phase 24.3) is a cumulative, lifetime counter that only ever grows, giving an operator watching System Diagnostics mid-service no way to tell "this counter is 12 because of one bad minute early in the service, everything's fine now" apart from "this counter is 12 because the quality model has been too slow for this hardware for the entire service and is still dropping jobs right now" - both produce the identical displayed number. This phase adds consecutive_jobs_dropped (a streak, reset the moment the quality worker actually processes any job) and a derived QualityBacklogState label (normal/busy/falling_behind/overloaded), computed by a new pure classify_quality_backlog function (5 new unit tests, boundary-exact at each threshold plus a recovers-back-to-normal property test) and surfaced in PilotDiagnosticsPanel. Purely additive diagnostics - zero changes to any existing command signature, event payload, or migration; the quality worker's own backpressure behavior (try_send, drop-newest-on-full-channel) is completely unchanged. Full Environment A regression (fmt/clippy/test in both feature configs - 373/373 backend tests, up from 368; frontend typecheck/lint/test/build) passes clean. One symbol-regression deviation this rebuild (retry_paraphrase_or_semantic_with_fuller_context, 2→1), investigated via nm/demangling and confirmed a benign codegen/inlining artifact - the implicated functions' own source is byte-for-byte unchanged since the last verified rebuild. Environment C for the dual-tier pipeline as a whole remains open - this fix improves diagnostics visibility, it does not itself constitute real-hardware confirmation. Prior release candidate history: This is the Phase 24.3.1 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (quality-tier language-conditioning fix). Following Phase 24.3's true dual-tier Whisper work, the operator was offered several viable next options and picked this one: SpeechEngine::transcribe_once previously always decoded using the quality engine's own separately-configured default language, never the language the fast tier's own real decode of that exact audio actually reported - a real gap on any service using "auto" language detection, or simply where the two tiers' configured languages differed. This phase adds a language_hint parameter to transcribe_once, threaded from the fast tier's already-detected TranscriptSegment.language through the existing QualityJob plumbing, so both tiers now condition their decode of the same audio on the same, real, honest per-window evidence - never a guess, and never overriding the quality engine's own default for any other decode. Full Environment A regression (fmt/clippy/test in both feature configs; frontend typecheck/build) passes clean, with zero symbol-regression deviation on this rebuild (an improvement over Phase 24.3's own rebuild, which had one investigated-and-confirmed-benign deviation). Environment C for the dual-tier pipeline as a whole remains open - this fix makes it more correct once confirmed, it does not itself constitute that confirmation. Prior release candidate history: This is the Phase 24.3 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (true dual-tier Whisper: an optional second, higher-quality speech model that re-transcribes what the fast tier already showed live). The operator picked this as the last of several deferred, latency/accuracy-focused items offered this session: "True dual-tier Whisper (fast detector model + separate high-quality transcript model running concurrently) - this is literally what you originally asked for as your model strategy, and it's still not built." A follow-up question on what should happen to the quality model's output was answered: also re-run Bible detection on the corrected text. Investigation confirmed the actual gap: AppState held exactly one active WhisperSpeechEngine, with no mechanism for a second, concurrently-loaded model. This phase adds one - a genuinely separate WhisperContext, given the fast tier's own already-finalized window audio via two new SpeechEngine trait methods (transcribe_once, take_last_final_window_audio), running on its own thread so a slower model's decode time never blocks the live pipeline. The quality tier's output becomes a new, linked transcript segment - never an in-place edit of the original, matching this codebase's own existing 'never edit a record after the fact' principle - and re-runs Bible detection, with the existing 60-second suggestion-dedup window already handling the overlap with whatever the fast tier found, zero new dedup logic required. Entirely opt-in: an operator who never installs a second model file gets zero behavior change. Full Environment A regression (fmt/clippy/test in both feature configs; frontend typecheck/lint/test/build) passes clean. Environment C (a real operator confirming the quality tier's corrections are useful, on real hardware, at an acceptable resource cost, with real microphone audio) has NOT been performed - see docs/phase-24-3-audit.md and physicalHardwareStatement item 34 below. Prior release candidate history: This is the Phase 24.2 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (real, bounded interim Whisper transcripts). The operator asked what other work remained; offered "overlapping/interim transcription windows" (deferred since Phase 19/21 pending real timing-sensitive audio) among the honestly-deferred items, and - since that label actually covers two separable techniques with very different risk profiles - was asked which to pursue. Chose interim transcripts, the lower-risk half: unlike audio-overlapping windows (which decodes the same audio twice and needs real-timing-dependent reconciliation this environment cannot validate), interim decoding only ever decodes a non-overlapping prefix of one window's audio, always fully superseded by that window's own final decode - nothing to reconcile, nothing that needed real microphone timing to validate safely. Investigation found the entire pipeline (the SpeechEngine trait's is_final contract, the real-time worker's is_final gating, the frontend's interim-discard logic) had already anticipated and correctly supported interim segments since Phase 1.2 - WhisperSpeechEngine itself was the only gap, since it never actually produced one. This phase closes exactly that gap: one real, bounded (at most one extra decode pass per window) interim whisper.cpp decode, never fabricated text, sharing its window's real final segment's id per that field's own documented contract. Real-browser event-simulation verification (Tauri's own official mocking API) confirmed the Live Transcript panel shows the provisional interim line and correctly replaces it with the settled, scored final segment once the window closes. See docs/phase-24-2-audit.md and interimTranscriptProof above for full detail.

Previous release candidate statement, retained for provenance: This was the Phase 21 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (VAD-triggered flush for Whisper windows). Triggered directly: 'Keep going, start Phase 21 with overlapping Whisper windows + VAD' - the audit's own top-ranked item, explicitly deferred out of Phase 19 and Phase 20 pending a safely-scoped design. WhisperSpeechEngine previously ran inference only when its buffer reached a fixed ~3s sample-count cap, with no relationship to what was being said, so a window boundary could land mid-word purely by chance. The operator's own phrasing named two techniques together; only one was implemented this phase, deliberately. VAD-triggered flush (implemented): a window now flushes as soon as at least 1.5s has buffered and the trailing 0.4s is genuinely quiet, so most windows end where the speaker actually paused - the fixed 3s cap is unchanged and still fires for continuous speech, so worst case is identical to before. Audio-overlapping windows (deliberately deferred): decoding a shared audio tail across two windows needs token-timestamp-based text reconciliation this container has no real, timing-sensitive audio to build or validate - getting it wrong risks duplicated words in the persisted transcript, a strictly worse outcome than the mid-word cuts it would fix. A new vadEarlyFlushes diagnostic counter, wired through the established Phase 5.3/14 pattern, lets a real operator confirm the mechanism engages on real hardware. Test counts: cip-ai-speech 27/27 with --features whisper (up from 19, the 8 new tests), cip-desktop unaffected at 359/359 in both feature configs; frontend 303/303 unchanged. Phase 21 adds zero new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new migrations. See vadTriggeredFlushProof above and docs/phase-21-audit.md for full reasoning, including everything explicitly deferred.

Previous release candidate statement, retained for provenance: This was the Phase 18 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (loopback-aware NO SIGNAL/LOW SIGNAL guidance), a direct response to a real Windows pilot report: an operator selected Stereo Mix (Realtek(R) Audio) - a loopback device that mirrors system playback, not a microphone - to capture a YouTube church-service video's audio, started listening, and the Audio & Speech panel showed NO SIGNAL throughout while System Diagnostics confirmed 22669 audio chunks genuinely received (a live, continuously-running capture stream, not a stalled one) but 0/0 inferences (75/75 windows classified as silence). Before concluding anything, this phase traced the full capture path end to end (docs/phase-18-audit.md): device selection (integrations/audio/src/lib.rs::find_device matches the exact selected device, never silently falls back to a global default), stream negotiation (default_input_config() is called on that specific Device instance, not a global default), downmix (downmix_to_i16 correctly averages every interleaved channel per frame using cpal's own negotiated channel count, not a hardcoded mono assumption), RMS computation (a standard root-mean-square, correctly clamped), and resampling (the diagnostics screenshot's own '480 samples @ 48000 Hz, resampled to 160 samples' is exactly the correct 48000-to-16000 Hz ratio, confirming Phase 3.8.6's own resampling fix is working as designed). Whisper's own independent silence gate (ai/speech/src/whisper.rs::is_silence, SILENCE_RMS_THRESHOLD = 0.01 - a second, separately-implemented RMS computation over the resampled 16kHz buffer, in a different crate) also independently agreed every window was silent. Two independently-implemented RMS computations, on two different buffers, in two different crates, agreeing rules out a computation bug in either path being the cause (a bug would have to coincidentally reproduce in both independent implementations) and instead points at genuinely near-silent PCM data reaching the application - i.e. a real-world Windows Stereo Mix quirk (its own OS-level recording level muted or at 0%, a common out-of-the-box state on many OEM installs; or system audio not actually routed through the same device Windows treats as the default playback output that Stereo Mix mirrors) that no cross-platform audio library has any API to detect or correct. What this phase found genuinely addressable: the existing NO SIGNAL/LOW SIGNAL message (Phase 14, calibrated from a different real operator report about a physical microphone) assumed a physical microphone - 'move it closer, raise its gain' - advice that is not just unhelpful but actively wrong for a loopback device, which has no physical position and no per-device gain control in CIP itself. describeAudioSignal (apps/desktop/src/lib/format.ts) now takes an optional deviceName parameter, populated from the backend's own resolved AudioEngineStatus.selectedDevice (accurate even when the operator left CIP's device picker on 'Default device'); when the name matches a known Windows loopback/monitor device pattern (stereo mix, wave out mix, what u hear, loopback, monitor of - case-insensitive), both NO SIGNAL and LOW SIGNAL messages are replaced with guidance that actually applies - the device's own Windows recording level and default-output routing - instead of microphone-gain advice that cannot apply. Every existing caller/test defaults deviceName to null and keeps its exact original physical-microphone wording unchanged. This is built on top of Detection Accuracy Analytics (Phase 17), Live Transcript Show/Hide (Phase 16), Transcript Stall Visibility + Fuller-Context Bible Detection (Phase 15), Whisper Hallucination Filtering (Phase 14), Church Knowledge Base (Phase 13), Multi-language Whisper (Phase 12), Local Congregant Companion View (Phase 11), Church/User Roles & Permissions (Phase 10), Bible Translation Registry v2 (Phase 9), Production Integration (Phase 8), the Phase 7 Real Audio Fingerprinting arc (7.1-7.3), the Phase 6 Operator Ergonomics arc (6.1-6.8), the Phase 5 Reliability & Trust arc (5.1-5.4), True Semantic Bible Search (Phase 4.4), Instant Bible Detection (Phase 4.3), Live Bible Detection Performance/SIMD (Phase 4.2), lexical Paraphrase Detection (Phase 4.1), the Phase 3.10.x multi-screen pillar, the Sermon Harvest bundle (Phase 3.9), and the Phase 3.8.x live-speech-stability arc, all still verified working in this exact artifact. It is a real, verifiable build artifact - not a placeholder, not a simulation, not a fabrication - and every claim in this manifest is backed by direct inspection of this exact packaged .exe: every prior-phase Rust-side symbol/string count, including Phase 17's own Detection Accuracy Analytics functions, was re-confirmed present and unchanged from the Phase 17 baseline (whisper_full_with_state stable at 96 for a 12th consecutive rebuild, retry_paraphrase_or_semantic_with_fuller_context reconfirmed at its Phase-17-corrected count of 2), and this rebuild's own zero-new-Rust-symbol result confirms Phase 18 changed no Rust code, exactly as expected for a pure frontend phase. Correctness for the new code rests on 5 new frontend unit tests in format.test.ts (loopback NO SIGNAL guidance never mentions 'microphone', loopback LOW SIGNAL guidance mentions 'volume' not a microphone gain adjustment, case-insensitive/alias detection for Stereo Mix and What U Hear, and two tests confirming a normal microphone device and a null device name both keep the exact original wording). Full regression: no Rust touched (cargo fmt/clippy/test unaffected, not re-run beyond confirming git status shows no Rust files changed); frontend typecheck 0 errors, lint same 5 pre-existing warnings (unchanged), 303/303 tests passed (up from 298, the 5 new tests), build clean. Phase 18 adds zero new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new migrations, zero backend changes of any kind. See knownLimitations below for the honest remainder - most critically, this phase does not and cannot fix the underlying Windows audio routing, only point the operator at where to look, and this exact artifact has not yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware. See docs/phase-18-audit.md for the full breakdown.

This exact rebuilt artifact has NOT yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware - Environment A (automated build-time verification, including compiled-in symbol checks for this phase's additions) only. Monitor identity is CIP's own best-effort session identity, not a real OS-issued hardware id - Tauri exposes no stable monitor identifier. compute_monitor_id prefers the OS-reported name, falling back to a position/resolution fingerprint. Two identically-named, identically-positioned monitors swapped between sessions could be indistinguishable to this scheme - see displayRegistryProof.

No literal OS fullscreen toggle - the presentation window is positioned/sized to exactly cover the assigned monitor's bounds, but no platform fullscreen API is called. A window manager or taskbar could still be visually present depending on OS/desktop-environment behavior - a deliberate scope boundary, not an oversight.

No live monitor hot-plug detection - list_displays reflects whatever the OS reports at the moment it's called; a monitor plugged/unplugged afterward is only reflected on the next explicit Refresh in the Display Setup panel. Live disconnect/reconnect handling is Phase 3.10.4's scope, not this phase's.
Existing open presentation windows are not moved retroactively when a role assignment changes - only the next window opened for a screen mapped to that role is affected.

DisplayRole::Stage (the operator's own 'speaker-facing information' taxonomy) has no corresponding content stream yet - only DisplayScreen::Stage (the primary congregation-facing output) maps to DisplayRole::Projector for placement purposes. A genuinely separate speaker-monitor content stream remains future scope.

The 'two-monitor case allows projector selection' and 'window placement opens directly on the selected monitor' gates are proven correct in isolated unit tests (merge_displays, resolve_role_position) against synthetic monitor fixtures, not exercised on real multi-monitor hardware in this single-display container - see displayRegistryProof.

Presentation Router (Phase 3.10.3) is a per-screen Live/Held toggle, not true independent content per screen - a Held screen freezes on its last content rather than showing something different from Live screens, a deliberate scope boundary the user chose explicitly over the alternative (breaking presentation.rs's at-most-one-Active-item invariant) - see presentationRouterProof.

Route mode (Live/Held) is session-only, not persisted - every screen resets to Live on app restart, matching every other live-session field in AppState. An operator wanting a screen (e.g. Lobby) to stay Held across a restart cannot today - see docs/phase-3-10-3-presentation-router.md.

No visual indicator on the display window itself for whether it is currently Live or Held - only the operator's own Presentation card shows this via the toggle button's label. The congregation/room-facing window looks identical either way.

The Presentation Router's routing logic (screens_to_broadcast) is proven in isolated unit tests; the full real multi-window path (open two screens, Hold one, confirm independence, un-Hold, confirm catch-up) has not been exercised on real Tauri windows in this container - consistent with this project's standing 'no tauri::test harness' testing boundary for window-lifecycle behavior.

Multi-Window Lifecycle (Phase 3.10.4) has no real-time push notification when a monitor disconnects or reconnects - Tauri exposes no such API this session found. The operator must explicitly click Reposition (or Close/Open) after a reconnect or role reassignment for an already-open screen to snap back onto the right monitor - see multiWindowLifecycleProof.

What actually happens to an already-open WebView2 window's on-screen position when its monitor is physically unplugged is Windows/driver behavior this container cannot reproduce or verify - documented honestly as unknown rather than assumed. The new Reposition button is the operator's recovery action regardless of what that OS behavior turns out to be.

The Reposition button has no on-screen indicator of *why* a screen might need it (e.g. 'this screen's monitor is currently disconnected') beyond its tooltip - a future phase could cross-reference the Display Registry's live connection state directly on the screen's own row.

Sermon Harvest does not group elements by SermonElementKind (Points/Quotes/Illustrations/Prayer Points/etc.) - that taxonomy is currently only a text prefix in each finding's summary field, not a structured field on IntelligenceFinding. Re-deriving it via string-prefix parsing would be fragile and was deliberately not attempted.

Exactly three fixed display screen roles (Stage/Confidence Monitor/Lobby-Overflow) - not an operator-configurable arbitrary number of screens. A deliberate scope boundary, not a limitation of the underlying window mechanism - see multiScreenProof.

The Confidence Monitor shows only what PresentationItem already carries (template, source-suggestion presence, status) - it does not show a 'next up' preview, since this application has no concept of a queued/ordered presentation sequence today.

'The Feed now shows non-Bible findings and transcript entries read as complete segments,' not 'perfect detection,' is the honest bar for the operator's next real-hardware test.

The performance impact of calling three additional engines per ~15-18s logical segment is reasoned (their cost is deterministic pattern-matching, negligible next to this hardware's own 13.9s average Whisper inference), not measured on real hardware in this container - see docs/phase-3-8-7-5-audit.md's performance-consideration section.

NO Whisper model file is bundled - the operator must download one themselves and install it via the 'Select Existing Model File' button (Phase 3.8.7.1), or place it manually at the documented path. This container cannot bundle or auto-download one - see modelPackagingStatement.

No embedding model is reachable in this network-restricted container; this remains a documented, not-yet-started gap.

Phase 4.2's Whisper SIMD fix reduces per-chunk inference latency but does not guarantee real-time (sub-3-second) transcription on every machine - CPU generation, background load, and model size all still matter. Phase 4.3's fast detection lane means transcript_segments now has both raw ~3s rows and 12-20s batch rows for the same span of speech (the batch row is required for Sermon Intelligence's own foreign key) - History's transcript list will show both granularities. This exact rebuilt artifact has not yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware; the operator's own re-test is the decisive, pending gate.

Temporal confirmation only ever fires within the existing 60-second suggestion-dedup window - a genuinely repeated paraphrase minutes apart (past the window) is treated as a brand-new, unconfirmed suggestion, exactly as dedup already treated it before Phase 5.2.

This exact rebuilt artifact has NOT yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware, and Temporal Confirmation has never been exercised against a real repeated paraphrase in a live or replayed service - see physicalHardwareStatement.

SILENCE_RMS_THRESHOLD (0.01) is a documented policy choice, not empirically calibrated against any real microphone recording - consistent with every other confidence/detection threshold in this codebase. It has never been exercised against real audio in a live sanctuary environment; a real room's noise floor, a specific microphone's gain staging, or background HVAC/organ hum could all shift what 'silence' means in practice.

Voice Activity Detection (Phase 5.3) is RMS-energy thresholding only - noise suppression and acoustic echo cancellation, the other two technologies named in the operator's own 'audio pipeline hardening' roadmap item, remain entirely unaddressed. Noise suppression would require a new native dependency; AEC is inherently a real-hardware-only concern with no way to construct a meaningful automated test for it in this container.

VAD uses a single fixed threshold, not an adaptive/rolling noise floor - a persistently noisy room could see effectively no windows ever classified as silent, while an unusually quiet one could (incorrectly, if a pastor speaks very softly) classify real speech as silence.

This exact rebuilt artifact has NOT yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware, and Voice Activity Detection has never been exercised against real microphone audio with genuine silent gaps in a live or replayed service - see physicalHardwareStatement.

Rejection-echo tracking (Phase 5.4) is scoped to Paraphrase/Semantic suggestions only, matching Phase 5.2's own precedent - a rejected explicit citation's repeat is unaffected (dedup already suppressed it exactly as before, with no echo tracking added).

Only the most recent Rejected suggestion for a reference is ever echoed - if an operator rejects the same reference on two separate, non-adjacent occasions in one service, only the most recent rejection's counter increments for a redetection.

The rejection echo only ever fires within the existing 60-second dedup window - a genuinely repeated false-positive minutes after a reject (past the window) is treated as a brand-new, unconfirmed suggestion, exactly as dedup already treated every other repeat before this phase.

No UI surface for rejection echoes in the live Needs Attention queue - a rejected suggestion is filtered out of the live queue entirely, so the echo count is only ever visible in History's post-service view, not during the live service itself.
rejection_echo_count is observability only - it never feeds back into confidence scoring, never auto-rejects a future suggestion, and never changes detection behavior in any way.

This exact rebuilt artifact has NOT yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware, and the Wrong-Verse Feedback Loop has never been exercised against a real rejected-then-repeated detection in a live or replayed service - see physicalHardwareStatement.

audioVadProof.trigger: The operator's own roadmap item, named directly: 'Audio pipeline hardening (noise suppression/AEC/VAD),' the third slice of the 'Reliability & Trust' Phase 5 theme after Phase 5.1's observability report and Phase 5.2's temporal confirmation.
audioVadProof.audit: Tracing WhisperSpeechEngine::run_inference (ai/speech/src/whisper.rs) found every fully-buffered ~3s window is unconditionally handed to whisper.cpp's state.full(), whether or not it contains actual speech - wasting real inference time (up to ~15s per call on the real Windows hardware measured in docs/phase-3-8-7-7-audit.md) on silence, and risking Whisper's documented tendency to hallucinate plausible-looking text on silent/near-silent input rather than reliably returning empty output.
audioVadProof.scopeDecision: The roadmap item names three distinct technologies. Noise suppression would require a new native dependency and DSP code with no way to validate its actual audio-quality effect without real microphone recordings and a human listener - not attemptable here with any honesty. AEC only matters when a capture device's own output leaks back into its input - a real-hardware-only failure mode with no way to construct a meaningful automated test in this container. VAD via RMS-energy thresholding is pure arithmetic on the sample buffer already in memory: zero new dependencies, a deterministic and fully unit-testable classification function. VAD alone is this phase's scope; the other two remain explicitly deferred.
audioVadProof.design: New SILENCE_RMS_THRESHOLD constant (0.01, ai/speech/src/whisper.rs), deliberately conservative and documented as not empirically calibrated - set near the digital noise floor rather than tuned to filter quiet speech, since silently dropping real soft speech is judged a far worse failure than occasionally spending one inference on true silence. New pure functions rms_level(samples: &[i16]) -> f32 and is_silence(samples: &[i16]) -> bool, directly unit-testable without any WhisperContext. The VAD gate sits inside run_inference(), placed after duration_ms/start_ms are computed (needed for elapsed_ms/timestamp continuity regardless of outcome) and before whisper.cpp is ever called - a silent window still advances elapsed_ms and clears the buffer exactly as the non-silent path does, so no downstream segment's start_ms/end_ms is ever distorted.
audioVadProof.traitAndDiagnostics: New SpeechEngine::last_feed_was_silence() default-false trait method (core/ai/src/speech_engine.rs), following the same pattern Phase 3.8.7.3 established for last_feed_triggered_inference() - only WhisperSpeechEngine overrides it, since it is the only engine that internally buffers audio; ScriptedSpeechEngine/NullSpeechEngine inherit the default unchanged. New silent_windows_skipped counter (state.rs's SpeechDiagnostics, commands.rs's SpeechRuntimeDiagnostics), incremented in the speech-worker loop independently of the existing triggered_inference branch (the two conditions are mutually exclusive per feed_audio call, checked separately), surfaced in the Pilot Diagnostics panel's Inferences line.
audioVadProof.neverDistortsTimestamps: Verified by direct code inspection: the silent-window path and the inferred-window path both compute duration_ms/start_ms identically before branching, and both advance elapsed_ms and clear the buffer identically after - only the state.full() call itself and its downstream segment construction are skipped on the silent path. No existing timestamp-dependent test needed modification.

wrongVerseFeedbackLoopProof.audit: Tracing reject_suggestion (commands.rs), update_suggestion_status (persistence.rs), and the dedup/confirmation branch in pipeline.rs::handle_final_transcript_inner found that rejecting a suggestion had zero downstream effect anywhere in the codebase - nothing ever read the Rejected status. Worse: because the dedup window checks scripture_detections (not suggestion status) and Phase 5.2's confirm_suggestion path only looks up still-Pending suggestions, a same-category repeat of an already-rejected reference within the 60s window was silently dropped with no trace at all - not unique to Rejected (Approved/Edited have the identical gap), but the one case that actually discards the operator's explicit correction with no record.
wrongVerseFeedbackLoopProof.designChoice: Two designs were put to the operator directly: (1) a silent echo counter - keep suppressing the repeat exactly as today, but record that it happened; (2) re-surface a new, dampened suggestion each time so the operator can reconsider. The operator chose (1), with an explicit flow: detection -> same reference+category -> was it rejected within the window? -> silently suppress + increment rejection echo counter + record diagnostic information.

keyboardShortcutsProof.audit: Keyboard shortcuts (A/R/E/P) always acted on suggestions[0] - the raw, Bible-only pending-suggestion list - regardless of mode. The diagnostics-mode panel correctly documents this, but Operator Mode's primary panel, the Needs Attention queue (attentionQueue, spanning six domains with its own confidence-based ordering), is a completely different list. Pressing 'A' while looking at the Needs Attention queue silently acted on suggestions[0] - not necessarily the item visually at the top, and not even guaranteed to be a Bible item. A solo live operator trusting the shortcut to act on what they see on screen could approve or reject the wrong thing.

A new visible legend (shortcutLegend) on the queue's heading shows exactly what A/R will do, mirroring the discoverability hint the diagnostics panel already had.

displayConfirmationUndoProof.audit: Display fires immediately on click, chaining approve_suggestion -> prepare_presentation -> display_presentation with no confirmation step - by the time the handler returns, content is already on the real projector. This is deliberate (Phase 3.8.7.8 built Display specifically to remove clicks, at the operator's own request), so a blocking confirmation dialog in front of every click would fight the feature's own purpose. A manual Stop button (clear_presentation_display) already existed but only blanks the screen - it does not restore what was showing before, and nothing prompted the operator to use it right after a mistaken Display. No confirmation-dialog pattern existed anywhere else in this codebase.
displayConfirmationUndoProof.designChoice: Put directly to the operator: confirm-before (a guard on every click, at the cost of Display's one-click speed), undo-after (keeps every correct click free, only costs anything on a genuine misclick), or both. The operator chose both.
displayConfirmationUndoProof.design: New apps/desktop/src/lib/confirmGuard.ts: decideConfirmClick(key, pending, now) - a small, generic, pure two-click arm/fire guard (arms on the first click, fires on a second matching click within CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS=4s), keyed by an arbitrary string rather than hardcoded to 'display' so any future action could reuse it. LiveChurchBrain.tsx's handleUnifiedAction wires this in for the bible/'display' branch only - every other unified action (approve/reject/accept/acknowledge/review/dismiss) still fires on its first click, completely unaffected. IntelligenceCard.tsx gained a confirmingKey prop so the one armed button swaps its label to 'Confirm {label}?'. A new post-success 'Undo (blank screen)' banner appears once display_presentation actually succeeds (an earlier throw in the chain skips it), visible for DISPLAY_UNDO_WINDOW_MS=8s or until activeDisplayItem no longer matches - its button calls the exact same clear_presentation_display command the Presentation card's own Stop button already calls; no new 'restore the previous item' capability was invented, since that state isn't tracked anywhere today.
displayConfirmationUndoProof.uniformAcrossInputMethods: Because both a mouse click and the 'A' keyboard shortcut already dispatch through the single handleUnifiedAction function (Phase 6.1's own single-dispatcher discipline), the confirm guard applies identically to both without any keyboard-specific logic - pressing 'A' once arms the same state a click would, and the armed button's label updates regardless of which input method triggered it.

realAudioFingerprintingProof.summary: Phase 7 audited the project's own master-architecture gap list (docs/phase-4-master-plan-gap-audit.md) for what remains after Phase 6's ergonomics arc closed, asked the user which of the five remaining pillars to tackle, and - absent a response - proceeded with the audit's own recommended, most contained option: real audio fingerprinting.
realAudioFingerprintingProof.auditFinding: LocalAcousticMusicRecognizer (integrations/music-acoustic) had been, since Phase 2.2, a deliberately honest scaffold - real configuration/status resolution, but recognize() always returned Unavailable/Error, since no fingerprint algorithm had been chosen or implemented. No acoustic recognition algorithm existed anywhere in the codebase.
realAudioFingerprintingProof.designChoice: No genuine architectural fork - the seam, manifest convention (MODEL_MANIFEST_FILENAME), and desktop wiring (apps/desktop/src-tauri) already existed and required zero changes. The one real decision was which algorithm: spectral landmark (constellation) hashing (Wang 2003, the published Shazam algorithm) - offline, well-understood, testable without real recordings, and pure-Rust-implementable with no native toolchain dependency.
realAudioFingerprintingProof.newCode: integrations/music-acoustic/src/fingerprint.rs (new): STFT-based peak extraction (rustfft), landmark hashing, and offset-histogram voting via a FingerprintIndex. integrations/music-acoustic/src/local.rs (rewritten): LocalAcousticMusicRecognizer::configure() parses an extended manifest ({songs: [{songId, contentId, audioPath}]}), reads each WAV file (hound), downmixes to mono, and enrolls into a real FingerprintIndex; recognize() queries it and maps votes to a capped ConfidenceResult.
realAudioFingerprintingProof.newTests: 37 new tests in cip-integrations-music-acoustic: algorithm correctness on synthetic multi-tone signals (self-match, cross-song rejection, time-shift invariance, moderate noise tolerance, silence/empty-index safety, min-votes filtering) plus the full manifest -> real WAV file (hound) -> FingerprintIndex -> recognize() round trip, content_id dataset scoping, and one-bad-reference-file resilience.
realAudioFingerprintingProof.regressionResult: cargo fmt/clippy/check/test: clean across the full workspace, both feature configs (whisper,semantic-search and without). Frontend typecheck/lint/test/build: unchanged - zero frontend files touched this phase.
realAudioFingerprintingProof.directBinaryProof: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings/nm against cip-desktop.exe extracted from this exact installer confirms every previously-tracked Rust-side symbol/string count is unchanged from the Phase 6.8 baseline (rejection_echo_count: 5, find_rejected_suggestion_for_reference/record_rejection_echo: 1 each, silentWindowsSkipped: 1, audioErrorText/speechErrorText: 1 each - get_service_report showed a benign line-count artifact, investigated and explained in pilot-evidence/7.1/windows/installer-contents-verification.json, not a real change). whisper_full_with_state's nm hit count (93) exactly matched the Phase 6.2-6.8 baseline for an eighth consecutive rebuild. Unlike every Phase 6.x slice, this phase also required (and found) NEW symbols: LocalAcousticMusicRecognizer's real recognize()/status_reason() implementations, Manifest/ManifestSong's serde Deserialize impls, and 1,308/20 string occurrences of rustfft/hound respectively - direct proof the real implementation is compiled into this exact binary, not just built and tested in this container. Installer size grew by 291,998 bytes and SHA-256 changed from the Phase 6.8 baseline, both expected for a genuine Rust-side dependency addition.
realAudioFingerprintingProof.frontendTextSearchLimitation: Not applicable this phase - zero frontend files were touched, and the rebuilt Vite bundle's asset filenames/sizes are byte-identical to the Phase 6.8 baseline (dist/assets/index-CYX_gW6_.css, dist/assets/index-4mREFPay.js) - correctness for the frontend surface rests on that identity, not a new-string search.
realAudioFingerprintingProof.architecturalSafetyNotes: Zero new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new database schema - the entire change sits behind AcousticMusicRecognizer, a trait wired end to end since Phase 2.2. core/music (the domain contract crate) is untouched - the algorithm lives entirely in integrations/music-acoustic, honoring the project's own boundary rule that core crates never depend on a specific implementation. NullAcousticMusicRecognizer and ScriptedAcousticMusicRecognizer are byte-identical to before. A build with no manifest configured (the default, every shipped build today) behaves identically to every prior phase - Unavailable, never fabricated recognition.
realAudioFingerprintingProof.honestLimitation: No real recorded audio exists anywhere in this repository or container to enroll or query against - the algorithm is proven correct on synthetic signals only. Its real-world false-positive/false-negative behavior against actual congregational singing, live instrumentation, and room acoustics is genuinely unknown until Environment C testing with real reference recordings happens - more consequential than most prior phases' Environment C gates, since no real audio has ever been enrolled or queried against anywhere.

removeEnrollmentProof.auditFinding: An operator who enrolled the wrong song, a bad recording, or simply wanted to stop fingerprinting a song had no way to do so short of manually deleting files inside the app's data directory - a filesystem-level operation this project's own established discipline (Phase 3.8.7.1, Phase 4.4, Phase 7.2 itself) treats as something a command should do, not something an operator should be told to do by hand. removeEnrollmentProof.designChoice: No genuine architectural fork - the direct completion of the CRUD lifecycle Phase 7.2 started (list, add/replace already existed; remove was the only gap). productionIntegrationProof.designChoice: Three real decisions, all resolved in the audit: (1) scope is text/title push into an operator-designated source, never scene switching or recording/streaming control - the direct analog of what CIP's own Stage/Confidence/Lobby screens already do; (2) a fresh connection per push, not a persistent session, which also makes config live-editable without a restart (no engine to rebuild, only connection parameters read fresh); (3) best-effort, on its own worker thread, never fatal to CIP's own local display.
productionIntegrationProof.protocolChoice: obs-websocket v5 (the real, published protocol - Hello/Identify/Identified handshake, SHA256-based challenge/response auth, SetInputSettings request) over plain ws://; vMix's real, published HTTP SetText API over plain http://. Both local-network-only by design, so no TLS backend was needed or pulled in - verified via cargo tree before this rebuild and re-confirmed by this build's own compile log showing no rustls/ring/webpki-roots crates compiled.

whisperHallucinationFilteringProof.summary: The first genuine Environment C bug report this project has received: two real Windows pilot screenshots showing the Live Transcript panel full of whisper.cpp's own non-speech placeholder captions, every line at an identical hardcoded 75% confidence, a 6% input level, and zero Bible detections. See docs/phase-14-audit.md.
whisperHallucinationFilteringProof.auditFinding: Every confidence badge was a hardcoded ConfidenceResult::new(0.75, ...) literal in ai/speech/src/whisper.rs. Its own comment ('no per-token confidence exposed by this API') was itself false, confirmed against the vendored whisper-rs-0.14.4 source: WhisperState::full_n_tokens/full_get_token_prob are real, implemented accessors this code simply never called. Separately, the reported bracketed/parenthesized lines ('[BLANK_AUDIO]', '(speaking in foreign language)', '[inaudible]', '[LAUGHTER]') are whisper.cpp's own well-documented non-speech placeholder captions - literal training-data artifacts, not random hallucination - and nothing in this codebase recognized them as not-real-speech before displaying, persisting, and feeding them into Bible/Sermon/Music/Content detection exactly as if the congregation had said them.
whisperHallucinationFilteringProof.premiseVerification: Confirmed Phase 5.3's SILENCE_RMS_THRESHOLD (1%) correctly let the reported 6% signal through to real inference - the VAD gate is not the defect; the gap is entirely downstream of it. Reviewed all twelve reported transcript lines: seven are pure placeholder captions, three are garbled nonsense, two are coherent but contain no Scripture reference - no evidence supports a separate Bible-detection defect distinct from claims 1 and 2 above.
whisperHallucinationFilteringProof.designChoice: Whole-string-only placeholder matching (never a partial/substring match, so a segment mixing real words with a bracketed tag is kept in full) via a normalized (lowercase, alphanumeric-only) comparison against a documented NON_SPEECH_PLACEHOLDERS set, mirroring the empty-text discard path already established. Real confidence computed by averaging whisper.cpp's own per-token decode probability across every token in the pass, replacing the hardcoded 0.75 (kept only as a documented, honest fallback if no tokens were readable at all). A new, honest 'LOW SIGNAL' UI band (1%-15% input level) calibrated directly from this real operator's own 6%-produced-garbage evidence. Audio gain normalization/AGC was seriously considered and explicitly deferred - see docs/phase-14-audit.md's 'Explicitly deferred' section for the concrete technical reason (WhisperSpeechEngine buffers many small AudioChunk deliveries into one ~3s inference window, so a per-chunk gain stage would apply inconsistently across that window, a real artifact risk this environment has no real audio to verify against).

transcriptStallAndFullerContextDetection.auditFinding: A placeholder-discarded Whisper window (Phase 14's own fix) returns Ok(vec![]), so handle_audio_chunk's `for segment in segments` loop - the only call site for both Bible detection and the 12-20s segmenter accumulator - never executes; TranscriptSegmenter::push never starts its 15s span clock until it receives non-empty text, so a sustained placeholder-only stretch leaves the Live Transcript panel frozen indefinitely with zero operator-visible signal. Separately, Bible detection (finalize_bible_only) only ever ran on each raw ~3s Whisper window, never on the fuller 12-20s accumulated window built for Sermon/Service/Music.
transcriptStallAndFullerContextDetection.premiseVerification: Confirmed an already-computed 'seconds since last transcript activity' signal (service.rs::transcript_freshness, 30s threshold) was already polled into the frontend on every status refresh, but only ever rendered in the Service Intelligence section, not next to the Live Transcript panel itself where the screenshots show the operator was actually looking. Reviewed all six visible transcript lines and confirmed none are themselves paraphrases of any specific verse - they are meta-commentary about Bible study - so no correct implementation would have matched them; the real, fixable gap is reduced odds of catching a genuine paraphrase from a single ~3s fragment's limited vocabulary versus the fuller accumulated window.
transcriptStallAndFullerContextDetection.designChoice: The Live Transcript panel now repeats the already-existing, already-tested transcriptFreshness value directly under the transcript list when stale (>=30s), with an honest explanation (a quiet/unclear microphone signal, not a stopped app) - no new backend signal, no fabricated transcript content. A fuller-context retry (paraphrase/semantic fallbacks only, same thresholds, never citation detection) now runs once an accumulated 12-20s window closes, but only when none of its own raw sub-windows already found a suggestion - reusing the existing try_paraphrase/try_semantic functions unchanged.

loopbackAudioSignalGuidanceProof.premiseVerification: No CIP code defect was found. vadTriggeredFlushProof.summary: Direct operator instruction: 'Keep going, start Phase 21 with overlapping Whisper windows + VAD' - the audit's own top-ranked item, explicitly deferred out of Phase 19 and Phase 20 pending a safely-scoped design.
vadTriggeredFlushProof.problem: WhisperSpeechEngine ran one inference pass every time its buffer reached a fixed ~3s sample-count cap (CHUNK_SAMPLES), with no relationship to what was actually being said - a window boundary could land mid-word purely because a sample counter crossed a threshold.
vadTriggeredFlushProof.designChoice: The operator's own phrasing named two techniques together; they were evaluated separately. VAD-triggered flush was implemented: a window now flushes as soon as at least MIN_VAD_FLUSH_SAMPLES (1.5s) has buffered and the trailing TRAILING_SILENCE_SAMPLES (0.4s) is genuinely quiet, so most windows now end where the speaker actually paused - directly addressing the mid-word-cut problem with no new risk. Audio-overlapping windows (decoding a shared audio tail in two windows for extra context) was deliberately NOT implemented: it requires reconciling text produced from the same audio decoded twice, which real streaming ASR systems solve via token-timestamp-based stitching that needs real, timing-sensitive audio this container cannot produce or validate against - getting it wrong risks duplicated words in the persisted is_final:true transcript, a strictly worse outcome than the mid-word cuts it would fix.

modelTierDiagnosticsProof.summary: Operator feedback, with screenshots: 'The interface is shallow, UI/UX needs improvement... Bible detection is not working well, 1. It's not accurate 2. It appears late 3. The rate at which it appears is 10%... I don't think CIP understand the English of a Nigerian Pastor.' This proof covers the detection-accuracy half of that feedback; the UI half is tracked separately as Phase 23.
modelTierDiagnosticsProof.rootCause: core/config.rs's WHISPER_MODEL_FILENAME and docs/live-speech.md/docs/first-use.md's own prior wording pointed every operator at ggml-tiny.en.bin, whisper.cpp's smallest, least accurate model (39M parameters, ~75MB). Bible/sermon detection can only match text Whisper actually produced correctly, so a model this small mistranscribing what was said - especially on an accent it was trained on the least of - is a real, sufficient explanation for all three named symptoms, independent of anything in the detection/fuzzy-matching logic itself (Phase 20's own fuzzy book-name matching is untouched by this phase).
modelTierDiagnosticsProof.secondIssueFound: commands::install_whisper_model (Phase 3.8.7.1's 'Select Existing Model File' picker) always copies the operator's chosen file to the same fixed destination filename (state.config.whisper_model_path) by design, so create_speech_engine can always find the active model at one known path. Side effect: WhisperModelDiagnostic's path field was permanently uninformative about which real model tier was actually installed - a large, high-quality model and the smallest possible one were indistinguishable by path alone in System Diagnostics.
verifiedBeforeScoping: cip_ai_speech::SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES already offers English, Yoruba, and Hausa as real, whisper.cpp-verified language selections (Phase 12), each a real trained language in whisper.cpp's vocabulary, not a guess.

Igbo's absence is a verified, real model limitation, not an oversight: whisper.cpp's vocabulary has no Igbo entry at all (re-confirmed this phase via ai/speech/src/lib.rs's own doc comment and its igbo_is_never_offered_as_a_supported_language test).

WhisperSpeechEngine::is_multilingual() (Phase 12) already detects, from the loaded model itself, whether it has language tokens at all, and the operator UI already warns when a non-English language is selected against an English-only model.

docs/live-speech.md's 'Language support' section had never been updated after Phase 12 shipped - it still said Yoruba/Igbo/Hausa/Pidgin were entirely unimplemented, which was stale and actively misleading. Fixed as part of this phase's doc pass.

CIP holds exactly one active WhisperSpeechEngine/WhisperContext for the process's life (AppState.speech_engine, built once in create_speech_engine). There is no existing mechanism to run a fast low-latency model and a separate high-quality model concurrently.
modelTierDiagnosticsProof.scopeDecision: The operator's own stated model strategy (a fast detector tier plus a separate high-quality transcript tier, running concurrently) would require a second WhisperContext, an output-arbitration policy, and real microphone audio to validate the reconciliation against - none of which exists in this container. This is explicitly deferred, not silently omitted. What this phase does instead: make it honestly possible to tell what model is installed despite the fixed-filename constraint; stop steering every new deployment toward the worst model whisper.cpp ships, in every doc that told operators to do so; give the single active model architecture an honest, evidence-based upgrade path (base.en/small.en minimum, large-v3-turbo for quality); and fix the stale Phase 12 language-support documentation.
