interimTranscriptProof.summary: WhisperSpeechEngine now runs one real, bounded interim decode per window, giving the operator's Live Transcript panel provisional text while a longer sentence is still being spoken, replaced by the settled segment once the window closes.
interimTranscriptProof.howItWorks: Once a window has buffered at least 1.5s (the same MIN_VAD_FLUSH_SAMPLES threshold Phase 21's VAD-triggered flush already used) without either flush condition firing, feed_audio calls the new try_interim_decode, which runs the exact same decode_pass (the real whisper.cpp full() call) the final decode uses, on just the audio buffered so far. At most one interim attempt per window (window_interim_decoded), so worst-case extra cost is exactly one additional decode pass, never unbounded. The interim segment shares its window's id with the eventual final segment, per TranscriptSegment::id's own documented contract.
interimTranscriptProof.whyNoRealAudioValidationWasNeededUnlikeO: Unlike audio-overlapping windows (still explicitly not implemented - see docs/phase-21-audit.md), interim decoding never decodes the same audio twice in a way that needs reconciling: it decodes a strict, non-overlapping prefix of one window's audio, and that prefix's decode is always fully superseded (never merged/stitched) by the final decode of the complete window.
interimTranscriptProof.frontendWiring: LiveChurchBrain.tsx gained interimTranscript state, set by onTranscriptUpdated on a non-final segment (previously simply discarded) and cleared once that window's final segment arrives or the service ends. Rendered as a dimmed, provisional trailing line in the Live Transcript panel. ServiceReplay.tsx was not touched - it never runs the real WhisperSpeechEngine.
interimTranscriptProof.realBrowserVerification: Headless Chromium using Tauri's own official @tauri-apps/api/mocks module (mockIPC/mockWindows with shouldMockEvents:true) rather than this session's earlier hand-rolled event stub - confirmed an interim TRANSCRIPT_UPDATED event renders the dimmed provisional line, and the same window's later final event (same id) removes it and adds the real, timestamped, confidence-scored entry to the permanent transcript list.
interimTranscriptProof.regressionScope: Zero new Tauri commands, zero new events. run_inference's final-decode behavior (window boundaries, VAD gating, silence handling, non-speech-placeholder filtering, confidence scoring, language detection) is bit-for-bit unchanged - decode_pass is the same logic, only relocated so try_interim_decode can reuse it.

dualTierWhisperProof.summary: CIP can now run a second, independently-loaded Whisper model (typically larger/slower than the fast tier) that re-decodes each fast-tier window's raw audio on its own thread, producing a new, linked transcript segment - never an in-place edit of the original.
dualTierWhisperProof.howItWorks: WhisperSpeechEngine now retains the raw i16 audio of its most recently finalized window (last_final_window_audio), exposed via the new SpeechEngine::take_last_final_window_audio. commands::handle_audio_chunk takes that audio for every genuine final window and, if a quality engine is configured and ready, try_sends a QualityJob to a bounded channel. spawn_quality_worker (its own dedicated thread) calls the quality engine's transcribe_once (the same decode_pass real inference the fast tier uses, run in isolation on the given audio, with no buffering/window state of its own) and, on a real non-empty result, builds a new final TranscriptSegment (fresh id, same timing/speaker as the original) and routes it through finalize_bible_only/finalize_and_route_segment - the exact same pipeline every other final segment uses, including re-running Bible detection per the operator's own explicit choice.
dualTierWhisperProof.whyNoInPlaceEdit: pipeline.rs's own documented principle - 'the transcript-and-detection record is never edited after the fact' - already applies to ScriptureDetection; Phase 24.3 extends the same discipline to transcript text. The corrected text lands as a new segment, linked to the original via a new transcript_corrections table (migration 0019), so what the operator actually saw live is never silently rewritten.
dualTierWhisperProof.backpressureDesign: The quality channel is small and bounded (capacity 4) with try_send (never blocking send) - a quality worker still catching up on a backlog (expected, since it is by design a slower model) simply drops the newest job rather than ever stalling the fast tier's own live pipeline or audio capture. speech_quality_diagnostics.jobsDroppedBacklog counts this honestly.
dualTierWhisperProof.optInDesign: The quality channel/worker are only ever created when state.speech_quality_ready is true (a real model successfully loaded from AppConfig.whisper_quality_model_path, installable via System Diagnostics' new 'Select Quality-Tier Model File...' button or CIP_WHISPER_QUALITY_MODEL_PATH). An operator who never installs a second model file gets zero new threads, zero new channel overhead, and zero change to the fast tier's own behavior.
dualTierWhisperProof.frontendWiring: LiveChurchBrain.tsx tracks corrected-segment ids via the new TRANSCRIPT_CORRECTED event and renders a small 'corrected below' badge on the original transcript line - the correction itself already appears as its own new entry via the existing TRANSCRIPT_UPDATED handling, unchanged. PilotDiagnosticsPanel.tsx gained a quality-tier section mirroring the fast tier's own layout (install button + live diagnostics).
dualTierWhisperProof.realBrowserVerification: Not performed this phase - judged not applicable the way Phase 24.2's frontend-rendering change was; this phase's real risk surface (two concurrently loaded Whisper models, a second thread, real audio hand-off) is exactly the class of behavior a headless-Chromium/mocked-Tauri-event harness cannot exercise. See docs/phase-24-3-audit.md.
dualTierWhisperProof.regressionScope: Zero changes to any existing Tauri command's signature/behavior, zero changes to any existing event's payload shape, zero changes to any existing migration - two new commands, one new event, one new purely-additive migration.
dualTierWhisperProof.environmentCStatus: Not yet performed - see knownLimitations and docs/phase-24-3-audit.md's own Known Limitations section for the full honest accounting.
dualTierWhisperProof.languageConditioningFix: Phase 24.3.1: transcribe_once gained a language_hint parameter, populated in commands::handle_audio_chunk from the fast tier's own already-detected TranscriptSegment.language for the exact window whose audio is being handed to the quality tier (via the new QualityJob.language_hint field). WhisperSpeechEngine uses language_hint.unwrap_or(&self.requested_language) for that one decode call only - the engine's own separately-configured default (self.requested_language) is never mutated. Closes the gap where the two tiers could silently condition on different languages for the same audio, most visibly under "auto" language detection.
dualTierWhisperProof.backlogVisibilityFix: Phase 24.3.2: SpeechQualityDiagnostics gained consecutive_jobs_dropped - reset to 0 by spawn_quality_worker the instant it dequeues and processes any job (a real correction, silence/placeholder, or even a transcribe_once error all count as evidence the worker is alive and keeping up), incremented by handle_audio_chunk every time try_send fails because the bounded quality channel is full. commands::classify_quality_backlog derives a QualityBacklogState (normal at 0, busy at 1, falling_behind at 2, overloaded at 3+ consecutive drops) - a streak rather than a duration, since quality jobs arrive as discrete, infrequent events (at most one per fast-tier final window) rather than a continuous stream the fast tier's own ms-based OverloadState/classify_overload measures. Purely additive diagnostics - never read by any decision-making code; the quality worker's own drop-newest-on-full-channel backpressure behavior is unchanged. See docs/phase-24-3-2-audit.md.

sessionBlackBoxProof.summary: CIP can now export a single downloadable JSON file bundling everything it observed during one service - the full transcript, full timeline, every suggestion, and every quality-tier correction - plus a plain-text human_summary paragraph, so an operator can hand back a complete record after a real test instead of a partial description.
